info.name: BranchWise Authentication API
info.description: Authentication endpoints currently defined by the BranchWise API contract. Requests and validation behavior can be exercised without MySQL. Successful registration requires a configured persistent AuthRepository backed by MySQL. Successful login additionally requires a persistent SessionStore and an atomic shared rate-limit store. Logout requires a live session plus a matching CSRF cookie and X-CSRF-Token header. The default application installs none of these adapters, so successful auth operations currently return 501. The fake adapters in pytest are test-only and are not available to Postman.

item.name: Register Owner and Business
item.description: POST /api/auth/register. Expected: 201 with owner_created/business_created true and branch_created false; 400 for invalid input; 409 for a duplicate email; 500 for a persistence error; 501 when no AuthRepository is installed. Production success requires the not-yet-configured persistent AuthRepository backed by MySQL. Registration does not create a session or branch.

request.description: Creates one Owner and one business atomically; it does not create a branch or log the Owner in. Requires the MySQL-backed persistent AuthRepository for successful production registration.

response.name: 409 Conflict — duplicate email
501 Not Implemented — no repository

item.name: Login
item.description: POST /api/auth/login. Expected: 200 with onboarding status and branchwise_session plus branchwise_csrf cookies; 400 for invalid input; 401 for invalid credentials; 429 when limited; 500/503 for persistence failures; 501 when required adapters are missing. Production login requires the not-yet-configured MySQL-backed AuthRepository, persistent SessionStore, and atomic shared rate-limit store. Postman retains the cookies for Logout. Import backend/postman/BranchWise-Local.postman_environment.json for baseUrl, owner_name, business_name, email, password, and csrf_token, or edit the collection variables in the Variables tab.

request.description: Successful production login requires MySQL-backed account lookup plus persistent session and shared rate-limit stores.

response.name: 200 OK — example success

item.name: Logout
item.description: POST /api/auth/logout. Expected: 200 after revoking a live session; 401 if unauthenticated; 403 if the CSRF cookie and X-CSRF-Token header are missing or do not match; 500 on revocation failure; 501 when no session manager is installed. Requires the same CSRF value in the branchwise_csrf cookie and X-CSRF-Token header. Keep Postman on the same host as Login so its cookie jar sends both auth cookies. Successful production logout requires the not-yet-configured persistent session adapter.

request.description: Sends the session cookie from Postman's cookie jar and the CSRF header captured after Login.

header.value: branchwise_session=; Expires=<past date>; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/api

response.name: 501 Not Implemented — no session manager
